Asset: WELL-0013 (SW-23 Well 013, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 24 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Mar 2023 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 25 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0013-0023 on 2023-03-23 Report written: 26 Mar 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0013-0023 at 11:15 on 2023-03-23 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.0% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.

  5. Excavated the stained soil.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0013-034

Asset: WELL-0013 (SW-23 Well 013, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 24 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 27 Jul 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 84 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0013-0194 on 2026-07-23 Report written: 28 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0013-0194 showed the wellhead at 38.1 °C with the air at 33.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.
